jobs.title: Talent Lead
jobs.description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

ElevenLabs has grown to over 1,000 in three years, and the rate of growth is not slowing down. As Talent Lead, you will be in charge of one of the most visible and impactful functions in the company: hundreds of hires a quarter across Research, Engineering, GTM and Operations, in one of the most competitive talent markets in history. You’ll move Talent from a high-volume recruiting engine to a strategic partner that tells leaders what is achievable, and you’ll rebuild how we hire using the same AI products we make.

You'll run the entire Talent team (currently 20 - 30 recruiters, sourcers, and talent operations) across verticals, setting the strategy, building the systems, and staying hands-on where it matters. You'll report directly to the Operations Lead and be a close partner to the People team. This isn't a pure executive role - we want someone who still loves the craft of recruiting and can model what great looks like for the team around them.

The right person has done this before at scale - at a company that grew fast and hired harder. Your team will look to you not just for direction, but as someone they can genuinely learn from. This will be an opportunity to shape the direction of Talent at ElevenLab; where we go, how we get there and who we get there with. If you want to shape the future of the Talent industry by building industry-defining playbooks using the latest technology and AI solutions, whilst building an expert team - this might be your best fit yet.

In this role you will:

  • Lead the full talent function across Research, GTM, Engineering & Product, and G&A hiring - setting strategy, managing team performance, building a recruiter capacity engine, and driving outcomes across all verticals.

  • Shape Talent Operations: ATS (Ashby) configuration, headcount tracking, hiring velocity metrics, and recruiter tooling - ensuring the function runs with precision and minimal friction.

  • Identify innovative ways of approaching Talent: design the next-gen Talent org structure, envision how Talent processes can be agentified and work with the team to build ElevenLabs products throughout.

  • Act as a strategic partner to department heads and hiring managers, bringing market intelligence, pipeline health visibility, and honest counsel on what it takes to consistently win the best people in the market.

  • Build and maintain a strong talent brand through thoughtful candidate experience, community engagement, building a Talent events program and creative sourcing strategies.

  • Coach and develop a team of recruiters, establishing clear standards for quality of hire, speed, and candidate experience.

  • Partner with functional leaders across Research, Engineering, GTM, and Operations - acting as a trusted advisor who can challenge, align, and mobilize leaders around talent priorities and workforce strategy.

We’re moving quickly on this search. Applications close on 13 November 2026, and we’ll start reviewing right away, so we’d encourage you to apply early.

Requirements

  • Proven track record leading large TA functions at high-growth companies, with direct experience filling hundreds of roles per year across multiple functions and geographies.

  • Hands-on recruiting instincts - comfortable being in the weeds on critical searches, not just managing from a distance.

  • Strong people leader who builds, develops, and retains recruiting talent.

  • Sharp on process: able to design and iterate on systems, tooling, and workflows that make a team of 20–30 perform at a high level with AI.

  • Close collaborator with People, Finance, and business leaders - comfortable operating at the intersection of headcount planning, compensation, and hiring strategy.

  • Held a high bar for quality of hire while hitting aggressive volume, with the metrics to show it.

  • Advised founders and executive suite on workforce planning, and changed a plan with your judgment.

  • Worked with Finance, People and RevOps on headcount planning, capacity modelling, compensation and offer strategy.

  • Has recruited across the Americas, EMEA and APAC and understands the differences between markets.

Location

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere, with the ability to operate from New York or London strongly preferred. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw.

We’re on a mission to open the world to everyone, giving our customers unlimited choice, unmatched ease and unmissable value for their next getaway.

Our trailblaze together culture is what drives our success, powered by our people and the way they work. Using progressive technology, we drive cutting-edge innovation and improve how our customers discover, book and experience their holidays. You’ll have the opportunity to accelerate your growth through meaningful challenges, new experiences and the freedom to shape your own path. You’ll create impact for our future by taking ownership, contributing to shared goals and helping shape what comes next, all as part of our enhanced international community of talented, collaborative and passionate teams.

The difference you’ll make

You’ll sit in the Product Marketing team, reporting to the Head of Product Marketing. You’ll work closely with our international commercial teams alongside Product, Design, Research, and Engineering to champion our international customers, identify what drives their booking choices, and uncover where loveholidays can win. Together, the team will turn customer empathy and market intelligence into high-impact proposition improvements and rapid experimentation that accelerate growth across key international markets, starting with a strong focus on Germany and the Netherlands.

The Product Marketing team acts as the critical bridge between local market dynamics and core platform execution. Collectively, the team combines qualitative customer research with deep commercial analytics to evaluate competitor models, diagnose performance gaps across the end-to-end booking journey, and define high-value opportunities that scale effectively across borders.

Product Marketing sits within our Platform function, which builds the technology and shared capabilities that power the loveholidays experience. By creating scalable products, systems and tools, Platform helps the wider organisation move faster, work more independently and deliver better outcomes for customers.

Your day-to-day:

International customer and competitor expertise

  • Build a deep understanding of customers in each international market: their needs, motivations, booking habits, expectations and barriers to choosing loveholidays. With a specific focus on Germany and the Netherlands.

  • Get hands-on with customer research, feedback and the end-to-end holiday journey, building real empathy and bringing the international customer’s voice into decisions across the business.

  • Understand competitor propositions and business models in detail. Experience their products, assess how well they meet local customer needs and identify where we need to close gaps or offer something more compelling.

  • Share customer and competitor insight broadly, helping teams distinguish between needs shared across markets and differences that require a local approach.

Market performance and opportunities

  • Understand performance by market, customer segment and stage of the journey, working with commercial and analytics teams to connect customer behaviour with conversion, repeat booking, customer satisfaction and commercial outcomes.

  • Identify where our proposition and experience are strong or weak, combining performance data with customer and competitor evidence to understand why.

  • Prioritise opportunities with clear recommendations on the customer problem, expected impact and how we will measure success.

Hands-on experimentation and improvement

  • Propose and run tests with international commercial and platform teams, taking opportunities from an initial hypothesis through to execution, measurement and a decision on what happens next.

  • Test changes to our proposition, messaging and customer experience, from how we explain our value to how customers search, book and manage their holiday.

  • Use results to refine our approach, stop ideas that do not work and build evidence for wider investment in those that do.

A platform that scales internationally

  • Translate international customer needs and market opportunities into clear proposition and experience requirements for product, design and engineering teams.

  • Work with platform teams to influence priorities and shape solutions that address local needs while building capabilities we can reuse across markets.

  • Identify where our platform limits international growth, including gaps in localisation, content, payment options, trust and the post-booking experience, and work with teams to test and address them.

  • Bring evidence from current markets into future market planning, helping teams understand what can scale, what needs to adapt and what we should validate before launch.

Your skillset:

  • You have significant experience in product marketing, proposition development, growth or a closely related discipline within a consumer-facing digital business, including work across international markets.

  • You are a customer expert. You go beyond research decks, spend time understanding real behaviour and can explain how needs differ between markets and customer segments.

  • You understand competition at the proposition level: why customers choose one provider over another, how different businesses deliver value and what that means for our own choices.

  • You are confident working with data. You can interpret market and customer performance, ask the right questions and combine quantitative and qualitative evidence into a clear point of view.

  • You have a track record of hands-on experimentation. You can turn an opportunity into a testable hypothesis, work with others to deliver it and use the results to decide what to do next.

  • You know how to work with product, design and engineering teams, translating customer needs into clear problems and requirements and balancing local relevance with platform scalability.

  • You communicate clearly and lead through influence. You build momentum across commercial and platform teams and challenge assumptions constructively.

  • You are comfortable moving between setting direction and doing the work. You bring curiosity, sound judgement and personal ownership of results.

  • Experience in B2C eCommerce is critical, travel experience is desirable

  • Fluency in one or more European languages, especially German highly desirable

The interview journey:

  • Intro with a member of the Talent Acquisition team - 30 mins

  • Virtual 1st stage with Hiring Manager - 45 mins

  • Final stage with key stakeholder/s including a task to present, in office - 2 hours

Perks of joining us:

  • Company pension contributions at 5%

  • Individualised training budget for you to learn on the job and level yourself up

  • Discounted holidays for you, your family and friends

  • 25 days of holidays per annum (plus 8 public holidays) increases by 1 day for every second year of service, up to a maximum 30 days per annum

  • Ability to buy and sell annual leave

  • Access to our electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme, season ticket loan and eye care vouchers

 

Our commitment to inclusion

At loveholidays, we focus on creating an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute, grow and succeed. We value the different perspectives, experiences and ideas each person brings, because they help us work better together, challenge our thinking and make stronger decisions.

As we continue to grow and evolve, we want everyone to feel supported and able to do their best work. We’re also committed to making our hiring process accessible, so please let our Talent Acquisition team know if you need any adjustments at any stage.

jobs.description:
In a nutshell: 4 to 6-month internship in our RevOps team at our Munich headquarters (hybrid), starting between February and April 2027, with the opportunity to move into a full-time role straight afterwards.

About this role at Luminovo

Luminovo builds the B2B SaaS platform that powers the electronics supply chain. DACH is our home market and one of our strongest, and we have recently expanded into North America and the rest of Europe.

GTM engineering at Luminovo is part of Revenue Operations, the department that sits between marketing, sales and customer success and makes sure our revenue organisation runs smoothly.

Our go-to-market engineering function builds the systems that find the right companies and the right people for our sales team: target lists, data enrichment, hyper-personalised outbound campaigns that signal our sellers whom to call next. We work closely with Account Executives, the BDR team and marketing and directly contribute to pipeline generation.

As our GTM engineering intern, you will run outbound campaigns end to end and help build the next layer: signal-based lead generation. You will also help us improve account scoring and build AI automations that take manual work off our sales reps.

There is no textbook for this role. You will learn it the way we did: by building, shipping and seeing what works.

By the end of your internship, you will have shipped revenue systems that our sales & marketing teams rely on every day, and gained hands-on experience in go-to-market engineering, one of the hottest roles on the market right now!

You will also see first-hand how a modern B2B start-up operates day to day, with AI built into its workflows.

This role is for you

  • You combine technical thinking with commercial curiosity: perhaps you studied engineering and want to understand how companies sell, or you have discovered a passion for the commercial side of start-ups.

  • You are keen to work in a fast-paced environment and to grow alongside a high-growth start-up.

  • You bring the drive to learn quickly, a sharp analytical mind and the ambition to take on real responsibility from your first weeks. You collaborate well, ask questions without hesitation and are happy to get your hands dirty.

  • You use AI as more than a better search engine. You have built your own automations, workflows or tools, and can explain what you shipped and what came of it.

  • You are fluent in both German and English. Much of our outbound targets buyers in the DACH region, while the company operates in English.

  • You stand out if you have built something entrepreneurial during your studies, be it a side project, a student society or a small business.

  • You have first experience in GTM engineering, sales operations or automation (this is a big advantage but not a requirement!)

Your performance objectives

🧬 Run outbound campaigns

  • Deliver multichannel campaigns end to end. Build target lists, source and enrich the right contacts, and write the messaging in German and English.

  • Go where coverage is thin. Your campaigns will go wherever our sellers need the most support or wherever there is an opportunity worth pursuing, starting with DACH and extending to the rest of Europe and North America. Take on event campaigns, new regions and opportunistic plays, and turn them around to contribute to our pipeline.

🌀 Build signals and tooling

  • Ship signals. Build plugins or scrapers that generate high-intent leads for our sellers.

  • Process scaling. Transform website engagement into automated outbound triggers and create repeatable playbooks.

⚙️ Build automations

  • Remove manual work. Automate the repetitive manual tasks our revenue teams deal with day to day.

  • Challenge what exists. Get to know the systems we have built, then tell us where they fall short and help improve them.

💶 Unblock the sales team

  • Understand what sales reps need. Work closely with our AEs and BDRs, get to know their accounts and processes, and remove the friction that slows them down.

You will learn to work with the most modern sales automation tools on the market, such as Clay, n8n, Twain, Lusha, Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator and many more.

Our Munich headquarters. For your first two months you will be in the office most days, so you get to know the product, the team, our ICP and the basics of our market. jobs.title: Fabrication Technician (Cleanroom) (Contract)
jobs.description:
About OLIX

AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The industry is still leaning on a ten-year-old hardware blueprint that has reached its limit. A new paradigm that is faster and more efficient will be the biggest economic opportunity of the next century and create the most important company of the next decade. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance.


About the role

This is a chance to get hands-on at the heart of a fast-growing AI hardware company. You'll run a micro-fabrication process flow in our London cleanroom, and the samples you make go straight into the prototypes our engineers are building for the next generation of AI infrastructure.

This role suits someone with excellent cleanroom discipline who takes pride in careful, repeatable work and wants to see it make a difference fast.


This is a 3-6 month contract role.


What you'll do

  • You'll run established process steps from written procedures, working closely with our process engineers

  • Run cleanroom process steps such as substrate preparation and photolithography, following SOPs exactly

  • Operate and look after process tools: routine checks, simple maintenance and flagging faults early

  • Inspect work in progress for defects using metrology tools and decide when to stop and escalate

  • Take routine measurements, such as thickness, surface profile and feature dimensions, to set methods

  • Prepare samples for test and hand them over to the engineering team.

  • Keep accurate run records so every sample is traceable

  • Keep the cleanroom running: gowning discipline, housekeeping, consumables, materials storage and safe chemical handling

  • Support engineers on experiments and report clearly what you observed


What you'll bring

  • Excellent cleanroom practice is the core requirement; we'll train you on our specific tools and recipes

  • At least one year of hands-on work in a cleanroom (ISO 7 or better), in industry or as a regular research cleanroom user

  • Practical fabrication experience: demonstrated ability to independently operate fabrication processes and record measurement results using metrology tools

  • Excellent contamination control: full-gowning, clean handling and working steadily in a cleanroom for long sessions

  • Careful defect inspection under a microscope, and the judgement to stop and flag a problem

  • Meticulous record-keeping: you follow SOPs exactly and write down what actually happened

  • Safe working with chemicals, hot equipment, UV light and lasers

  • Right to work in the UK, and eligibility under the export-control conditions below


Nice to have

  • Experience across several process areas, such as coating, bonding, wet processing, deposition or etch

  • Metrology: stylus or optical profilometry, confocal microscopy and thickness measurement

  • Work in a production or pilot-line setting (semiconductor, MEMS, PCB, display or medical devices) as well as in R&D

  • A degree, or study towards one, in physics, materials science, chemistry or engineering

  • Simple data handling in Excel or Python for run logs and SPC charts


Due to U.S. export control regulations, candidates’ eligibility to work at OLIX depends on their most recent citizenship or permanent residency status. We are generally unable to consider applicants whose most recent citizenship or permanent residence is in certain restricted countries (currently including Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Belarus, China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Venezuela). Applicants who have subsequently obtained citizenship or permanent residency in another country not subject to these restrictions may still be eligible.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Operations Research
jobs.description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

What you'll do

CircuitHub builds circuit boards on demand, every order different. Each day thousands of decisions are made: which orders run on which machines, which parts to buy and when, what to promise a customer and what to charge. You'll build the models behind those decisions.

  • Plan the factory. Schedule orders, panels and machines across our factories for throughput and on-time delivery, and know days ahead when we will run out of work or capacity.

  • Model the Grid. The Grid is our factory-scale robot: dozens of movers, gantries, printers and ovens. Model how work flows through it, find the bottlenecks, and tell us what the next machine or change is worth.

  • Price and promise. Estimate what an order really costs in labour, machine time and parts, and help set prices and lead times that win work and make money.

  • Buy smarter. Decide what parts and consumables to stock, when to order them, and how much risk of a shortage to accept.

  • Put it into production. Your models don't live in a spreadsheet: they run every day, feed the planning and quoting systems, and get checked against what actually happened.

What we look for

  • A quantitative background in operations research, applied maths, statistics, quantitative finance, economics or a similar field, and a record of models that changed real decisions.

  • Optimisation: linear and integer programming, constraint programming, or heuristics, and judgement about when a simple rule beats a solver.

  • Simulation and forecasting: building a model of a messy system, calibrating it to data and saying how far to trust it.

  • Strong Python and SQL. You write code other people can run and rely on.

  • You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

  • Curiosity about how things are physically made. You'll spend time in our factories in the US and UK.

Manufacturing experience is welcome but not required. If you have priced risk, optimised a portfolio or forecast demand, the problems here will feel familiar.

Stack

  • Modelling: Python, OR-Tools, simulation

  • Data: PostgreSQL, Snowflake, dbt, Dagster

  • Agents: Claude Code and Codex throughout

Location

Remote anywhere, or from our offices in London or Cambridge (UK) if you prefer, with regular visits to our factories in the UK and US.

Pay

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

Remote within the UK, or from our offices in London or Cambridge if you prefer.

The opportunity

CircuitHub is trying to solve a difficult problem: why can software engineers iterate almost instantly while hardware engineers can still wait weeks or months to manufacture a new design?

The company was founded by engineers who had experienced that frustration first-hand. What began as software to make ordering electronics easier has evolved into a much more ambitious manufacturing platform, combining software, robotics and automation to redesign the production process itself.

Today CircuitHub operates an automated electronics manufacturing platform serving hardware businesses across areas including robotics, autonomous systems and other advanced technology applications. Its proprietary Grid system is a factory-scale robotic assembly platform designed for rapid, high-mix electronics production.

The business is now scaling quickly. CircuitHub has raised $45 million to expand manufacturing capacity in both the US and Europe, building on operations in Massachusetts and its growing UK presence. Cambridge is becoming an increasingly important hub alongside London and the company's distributed team.

That growth creates a corresponding need to strengthen the operating infrastructure behind the company. Finance is one of the areas where CircuitHub has deliberately remained lean for longer than it probably should have.

Context: where finance is today

The finance team is led by a Finance Director and Management Accountant, both experienced, qualified accountants. This role brings dedicated financial accounting and technical reporting capability into the team, taking ownership of the books, the audit and the technical questions that come with a growing international group.

CircuitHub uses NetSuite to operate its inter-company financial model across the UK and US. A significant amount of day-to-day UK finance activity is outsourced, while the internal team takes greater ownership of the larger US operation, group reporting and consolidation. This role will be the main point of contact for the outsourced firm, reviewing their work and making sure it meets the standard the group needs, while also working across the US side and the wider mechanics of an international business.

Just as importantly, CircuitHub is thinking carefully about what the next generation of finance roles should look like. AI and automation are already being deployed across the company, including in areas where repetitive finance work can be made considerably more efficient.

That makes strong technical accountants even more important. CircuitHub needs people who understand the numbers well enough to judge whether automated output is right, and who can use technology to improve how finance works without weakening control.

That combination of technical accounting, real ownership and a technology-enabled way of working is a central part of the opportunity.

The mandate

The Group Financial Accountant will take ownership of CircuitHub’s financial accounting across the UK and US. That means understanding how the books are put together, running a reliable close and being the person the Finance Director, the auditors and the outsourced accounting firm rely on for accurate, well-supported numbers.

Alongside the core accounts, the role will lead on technical accounting as the business scales. CircuitHub is investing heavily in manufacturing capacity and moving towards more flexible commercial models, which raises questions around revenue recognition, capitalisation and intercompany that need a clear owner.

The candidate must be willing to get their hands dirty to get a full appreciation of the sales cycle & work with the Finance Director to improve our systems and controls to improve our collection cycle, reducing DSO & further automation for our credit offering.

The candidate should have a good technical understanding in accounting that can lead to developing financial operations without complicating or delaying the reporting process. Developing our systems to improve the speed and efficiency of areas such as revenue recognition, R&D capitalisation & the consolidation process.

What you will work on

The precise balance will evolve with the candidate, but the remit is expected to include:

  • Financial accounting and close. Own month-end, including journals, accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations, with a clear understanding of how the accounts fit together.

  • Audit and statutory reporting. Act as the first point of contact for the auditors, manage their requests and prepare supporting schedules under UK GAAP and IFRS.

  • Technical accounting. Lead projects such as IFRS 15 revenue recognition, the capitalisation policy and the treatment of intercompany transactions as the business and its commercial models develop.

  • Group reporting. Support reporting across the UK and US entities, including intercompany reconciliations, and contribute to group consolidation in NetSuite where experience allows.

  • Outsourced provider management. Manage the relationship with the UK outsourced accounting firm, reviewing their output and holding it to the standard the group needs.

  • NetSuite and finance systems. Work directly in NetSuite and across the different systems and platforms that feed into it. Understand how data moves through the business rather than treating the accounting system in isolation.

  • AI and automation. Review and take ownership of automated and AI-generated finance output, making sure it is accurate and properly controlled, and help identify where further automation makes sense.

What success looks like

The first objective is to be a safe pair of hands. That means solving outstanding technical issues, taking ownership of monthly & quarterly close, a well-run audit and numbers the Finance Director and the team can trust without needing to revisit them.

From there, success means taking ownership of the technical agenda: a clear approach to revenue recognition as commercial models change, a robust capitalisation policy as CircuitHub invests in capacity, and clean intercompany accounting across the UK and US.

Over time, the finance team should have the capacity to report more frequently, stronger oversight of outsourced work and less technical accounting sitting with the Finance Director simply because nobody else can own it.

Processes should improve as well as move faster. Automation should remove low-value work without weakening financial control.

This is a role to build into over time. The scope will grow with the finance function and with the contribution the individual makes to it. As the business scales, the role is expected to grow into Group Financial Controller.

The person we are looking for

CircuitHub is looking for a qualified or near-qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA) with strong technical foundations. The specific qualification matters less than acumen, drive and personal qualities.

You are likely to have trained in practice, whether at a Big 4 or a top 20 firm, and be looking for your first move into an operating business. Alternatively, you may already be working in industry, in which case you will be qualified or close to qualifying.

The strongest signals are:

  • Relevant exposure. Experience getting the most out of NetSuite, working in a finance team to produce accounting information & ability to work autonomously and conscientiously to meet deadlines.

  • Technical grounding. Strong knowledge of UK GAAP and IFRS and a clear understanding of how a set of accounts is put together.

  • Technology fluency. You are comfortable working across systems and genuinely interested in how AI is changing finance. You see automation as a tool, not a substitute for judgement.

  • Practical curiosity. When something does not reconcile or a process feels unnecessarily difficult, your instinct is to understand why.

  • Commitment to building. You are motivated by breadth and ownership, and you want to build something over time in a growing business.

  • Interest in the business. CircuitHub sits at the intersection of software, robotics and physical manufacturing. You do not need an electronics background, but an interest in technology and how real products are built will make the environment much more compelling.

Why CircuitHub

This is a chance to join a profitable, fast-growing robotics and manufacturing business at a pivotal stage of scale, in a role with genuine technical ownership.

You will work closely with experienced qualified accountants and gain a breadth of exposure that is rare this early in an industry career: revenue recognition, capitalisation, intercompany, audit and reporting across a UK and US group.

You will also build for where finance is going next. CircuitHub is already using AI, automation and connected systems across the business, creating the opportunity to combine strong technical accounting with skills in systems, data and automation.

For someone with the capability and drive, there is real scope to grow as CircuitHub scales and the finance function builds out around it.

Pay

£75k–£85k, depending on experience, plus equity.

jobs.title: Senior Frontend Engineer, Marketing Website
jobs.description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

The Role

As a Senior Frontend Engineer on our Website team, you'll be a co-owner of the platform behind synthesia.io: the component library, content model and rendering stack that every page on our marketing site is built from. You'll shape direction and make key technical decisions with the team, likely with a focus area of your own but context across the whole system. This is a hands-on engineering role, and your primary output is high-quality component and schema code, plus the tooling that lets others build with it.

Millions of people visit synthesia.io every month, and it is one of the main ways we win new customers. That comes with real responsibility. The decisions you make are seen at scale, and we set the quality bar accordingly.

The defining challenge of this role is composability: a marketing site that marketers, and increasingly AI agents, can build pages with, without breaking design, performance or SEO.

What You'll Do

  • Build, scale and evolve our section library: the Astro components, Sanity schemas and design tokens that let us compose marketing pages consistently and accessibly.

  • Own the content model. Design schemas that resist misuse, so an editor, or an agent, can build a page that is correct by construction rather than correct by review.

  • Take Figma component specs all the way to production: responsive across mobile, tablet and desktop, accessible by default, matching design intent precisely.

  • Extend the platform for AI-assisted development, so coding agents can generate on-brand, on-spec sections from a design spec as reliably as a person can.

  • Own SEO integrity as a first-class engineering concern: canonicals, sitemaps, structured data, redirects, and no traffic cliffs on launch.

  • Raise the bar on engineering standards across the website surface: thorough code review, patterns others can follow, and tests around the parts that actually break.

  • Maintain and extend localisation across nine locales and a translation pipeline, so the system works for a global audience.

  • Shape the technical direction of the website platform over the next 6 to 12 months, and champion its adoption with the people who publish on it.

We’d love to hear from you if you have

  • At least five (5+) years as a software engineer, including three (3) at senior level, building front end for content-driven or marketing platforms.

  • Real ownership of a content model in Sanity. You've designed schemas other people had to live with, and you have opinions about references vs. embedded objects, when a variant belongs in the schema versus at runtime, and how to stop a section library sprawling. GROQ and Portable Text are familiar territory.

  • Deep front-end expertise: expert HTML, CSS and TypeScript, with a strong command of component API design and the developer experience of a shared library.

  • You can work end to end. Comfortable owning the server side as well as the front end: SSR, serverless and edge runtimes, API routes, a SQL database, secrets and CI. You should be able to take a feature from schema to component to the route that serves it without handing off, and be happy debugging something that only reproduces in production.

  • Solid understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility and web performance, and comfortable building to WCAG 2.2 AA. Accessibility is part of your definition of done, not a separate pass.

  • You care that marketing sites are measured, on performance, SEO, analytics events and conversion, and you're happy being accountable to those numbers.

  • A strong sense of craft and attention to detail, and the judgement to balance design intent against engineering constraints.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills. You explain your reasoning, review generously, and treat levelling up the people around you as part of the job.

We’d be particularly excited if

  • Prior experience working on a large SaaS marketing website, at real traffic and with real stakes attached.

  • Astro, or another islands or static-site framework.

  • Cloudflare Workers, or another edge or serverless platform.

  • Experience with AWS Lambda.

  • Tailwind CSS v4, and experience working from a token-based design system.

  • Experience, or strong interest, in making component libraries and content models consumable by AI agents.

  • A strong design sensibility: an eye for visual detail and the judgement to push back on and improve design decisions, not just build them.

  • Experience with localisation and internationalisation at scale for a global audience.

  • Analytics and tag management implementation: dataLayer events, server-side tagging, getting attribution right without hurting performance.

Location
Our preference is for this role to be based hybrid out of our London, UK office. We can also accommodate remote workers elsewhere in Europe subject to compliance and right to work checks.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

As Head of Financial Controller, you will own the full accounting function across Filigran's entities, including revenue recognition, consolidation, monthly and year-end close, and internal controls. General Accounting Operations

  • Own the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of all financial transactions across Filigran entities

  • Continuously improve a scalable monthly/quarterly close process

  • Ensure revenue recognition is correctly applied and documented

Multi-Entity Oversight

Leadership & Cross-Functional Support

  • Proven ability to build processes and internal controls from scratch in a fast-growing or scaling environment

jobs.title: DevOps Engineer
jobs.description:
For this role, we will only consider candidates who are currently based in the Netherlands.

About SkinVision

Skin cancer is highly treatable when caught early, but limited access to specialist care and long wait times delay diagnosis, increasing the risk of late-stage cases and driving up treatment costs. SkinVision, founded in Amsterdam in 2012, exists to close that gap. Our proprietary AI — certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU regulation, with over 90% sensitivity and 89% specificity — has already helped nearly 3 million people worldwide detect early signs of skin cancer. Today, SkinVision has a database of more than 6 million skin spot assessments and can reach 20 million people through insurer partnerships. High-risk cases are reviewed by a team of dermatologists, who support users in taking the right next step — from urgent care to a specialist referral. We are extending this further, connecting users faster to the specialist care they need. We're a focused, international team, active globally, united by one goal: making early detection accessible to everyone, everywhere. If you join us, you're not just building a product — you're helping close the gap between a person noticing something and getting the care they need.

DevOps at SkinVision

As a DevOps Engineer at SkinVision, you will play a key role in building, scaling, and securing the infrastructure that powers our AI-driven health platform. You’ll design and maintain our cloud-based systems in AWS, implement CI/CD pipelines, enhance observability using Datadog, and drive operational excellence through automation and monitoring.

Your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of a medical-grade system that serves users globally. You’ll collaborate closely with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure smooth delivery, rapid deployments, and resilient operations — ultimately enabling us to deliver life-saving technology with confidence.

Beyond hands-on expertise with AWS and modern DevOps tooling, we’re looking for someone who thinks architecturally. You’ll get to know our current setup, form your own view of how it should evolve, and help define a target vision for our infrastructure, then drive its implementation. Day-to-day operational work is part of the role, but we value someone who thinks before building and takes ownership of where our infrastructure goes next.

What you will do

Cloud Infrastructure & Automation

  • Design, build, and manage AWS-based infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency.

  • Implement and manage infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation.

  • Automate environment provisioning, configuration, and deployments using CI/CD pipelines.

  • Ensure system resilience, security, and performance through automated monitoring and alerting.

CI/CD & Deployment

  • Design and optimize CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, reliable, and safe deployments across environments.

  • Manage deployment workflows using Argo CD and Kubernetes.

  • Collaborate with developers and ML engineers to streamline build, test, and release processes.

  • Integrate automated testing, rollback strategies, and version control into the deployment lifecycle.

Observability & Monitoring

  • Build a comprehensive observability stack using Datadog for metrics, logs, traces, and alerts.

  • Define service-level objectives (SLOs), service-level indicators (SLIs), and dashboards for system performance.

  • Proactively detect and resolve performance bottlenecks, capacity issues, and reliability risks.

  • Create automated health checks and ensure visibility across production systems.

Security & Compliance

  • Implement security best practices for AWS, containers, and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Manage identity, access, and secret handling (IAM, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store).

  • Ensure compliance with medical device standards and data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA).

  • Partner with the Information Security Officer to embed security controls across infrastructure and deployments.

Reliability & Incident Management

  • Lead incident response and root cause analysis for infrastructure or deployment-related issues.

  • Establish SLAs and operational runbooks for production environments.

  • Continuously improve system reliability through chaos testing, redundancy, and fault tolerance.

  • Mentor engineers on DevOps principles, observability practices, and infrastructure automation.

Infrastructure Strategy & Architecture

  • Assess the current infrastructure and deployment setup, and form a well-reasoned view of how it should evolve.

  • Define and maintain a target architecture for our cloud platform, balancing reliability, scalability, security, and cost.

  • Translate the target vision into a practical roadmap and drive its implementation incrementally, alongside day-to-day operations.

  • Document and communicate architectural decisions, aligning with engineering and leadership on technical direction.


Essential skills

  • Minimum of 6 years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Infrastructure roles.

  • Strong expertise with AWS services (EC2, ECS/EKS, S3, RDS, CloudWatch, Lambda, etc.).

  • Expert in Kubernetes and Argo CD, deploying and managing production-grade custom Helm charts with secure, automated GitOps workflows in EKS

  • Advanced knowledge of CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar).

  • Proficiency in Datadog for observability, monitoring, and alerting.

  • Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, Bash, or Go.

  • Experience managing infrastructure with Terraform, CloudFormation, or Ansible.

  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals, load balancing, and API gateway configuration.

  • Excellent problem-solving and incident management skills.

Desirable skills

  • Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, MedTech, or FinTech.

  • Familiarity with multi-environment architecture (staging, pre-prod, production) and blue-green deployments.

  • Exposure to event-driven systems, message queues, and data streaming (Kafka, SNS/SQS).

  • Understanding of Zero Trust networking and cloud security best practices.

  • Experience in cost optimization and performance tuning in AWS.

Qualifications

  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

  • Certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), or Terraform Associate are a plus.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary, additional benefits, and a hybrid working policy

  • A vibrant, dynamic, and rapidly growing scale-up in Amsterdam

  • An enthusiastic, professional, and international team

  • Regular team events, including off-sites and fun activities

  • Unlimited skin checks for you

About AIHR

Founded in 2016 with the mission to future-proof HR, the Academy to Innovate HR (AIHR) has become the world’s market leader in online training for human resources (HR) professionals. We have a global customer base spread across 140+ countries, amongst which companies like Unilever, Reckitt, Goldman Sachs, Philips, Deloitte, Nike, Heineken, and UBS. It is our goal to continuously upskill and empower 1,000,000 HR Professionals.

We are an international team of 100+ people, driven by excellence, innovation, and a hunger to grow in everything we do. As such, we strive to provide the world’s best courses and excellent support to our customers while continuously optimizing every aspect of our work. With over 30 nationalities, our team is diverse, yet we all share a few traits: we're friendly, enthusiastic, and great team players.

Being a fast-growing company, working at AIHR means taking on a lot of responsibility and getting countless opportunities to develop yourself in new areas and the potential to craft your own role.

Role and Responsibilities

As our Senior Growth Marketing Manager, you'll play a key role in accelerating customer acquisition across our B2C and B2B businesses. Working closely with the Head of Growth Marketing and VP of Marketing, you'll help us achieve our ambitious growth targets, improve acquisition efficiency, and identify new opportunities to scale.

A core part of your role will be diving into performance data to understand what's working, what's not, and where our biggest growth opportunities lie. You'll work closely with our Performance Marketing Specialist to scale paid acquisition, challenge existing strategies, test new approaches, and support campaign execution where needed. You'll also collaborate with our CRO Specialist to identify opportunities across landing pages, website journeys, and conversion funnels, turning insights into experiments that drive more leads and revenue.

You'll bring a strong growth perspective to our email marketing efforts, working with the team to analyze nurture flows, promotional campaigns, and audience segments, and identify opportunities to improve performance. Beyond optimizing existing channels, you'll explore, launch, and scale new acquisition opportunities, including those emerging from the changing AI- and LLM-driven marketing landscape.

Most importantly, this is a hands-on role where you'll do more than develop strategies and bring ideas to the table. You'll actively execute initiatives yourself or work closely with the wider team to bring them to life. Whether you're launching a new campaign, testing an acquisition channel, or improving conversion, you'll take ownership of turning opportunities into measurable business results.


On a typical week

It's Monday morning, and you start the week with a coffee and a look at last week's acquisition performance. You open GA4, HubSpot, and your marketing dashboards to see how we're tracking against our B2C and B2B MQL targets. While digging into the data, you notice that one of our paid campaigns is generating plenty of traffic, but conversions have dropped. You investigate further, identify a few potential causes, and head into the Growth Marketing stand-up with some ideas to improve performance.

After the stand-up, you catch up with our Performance Marketing Specialist to review campaign performance and discuss opportunities to scale. You identify a promising new audience and agree to test a different creative approach. Rather than just handing over your ideas, you jump into the advertising platform to help set up the campaign and work with the team to get the new creatives ready for launch.

On Tuesday, you're focused on improving our B2B acquisition funnel. You've spotted an opportunity to increase conversions on the AI for HR Boot Camp landing page. You meet with our B2B Marketer and CRO Specialist to review the data, discuss your hypothesis, and agree on an experiment. You brief the team, align with sales on the proposed changes, and help move the experiment towards launch.

Wednesday is a work-from-home day, giving you time to dive deeper into our acquisition strategy. You've been exploring how AI and LLMs are changing the way HR professionals discover training providers. You identify a potential new acquisition opportunity, research the market, and put together a practical plan to test it. Later, you meet with the Head of Growth Marketing to challenge your assumptions, refine the approach, and agree on the next steps.

On Thursday, you review the performance of our B2C email nurture flows with the Email Marketing team. You notice an opportunity to improve conversions from leads to MQLs and propose a change to the messaging and sequence. After lunch with colleagues in the office, you turn your attention to an upcoming quarterly campaign, working with the wider Marketing team to finalize the messaging and coordinate the launch. You also start investigating new channels that could help expand the campaign's reach and attract new audiences.

Friday starts with reviewing the results of a recent landing page experiment. The changes have improved conversion, so you work with the CRO Specialist to roll them out more broadly. You also catch up with our BizOps team to improve HubSpot reporting, ensuring we have better visibility into acquisition performance and opportunities for growth. Before wrapping up the week, you review progress against our growth priorities, share your findings with the team, and identify the next opportunities worth pursuing.

After a productive week of analyzing, experimenting, and driving initiatives forward, you close your laptop and join your colleagues for Friday drinks.

jobs.description:
wo-afstudeerstage/praktijkstage, vanaf februari 2027

Ben jij die nieuwsgierige onderzoeker die energie krijgt van data, duurzaamheid en nieuwe inzichten?
Wil jij een inhoudelijke bijdrage leveren aan de statistieken van het CBS?

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het kabinet wil dat Nederland in 2050 volledig circulair is. Om te kunnen volgen of we die doelstelling halen, is betrouwbare informatie nodig over onder andere afval en emissies naar water. Het CBS verzamelt en publiceert deze gegevens voor bedrijven. Daarbij maken we vooral gebruik van gegevens uit het elektronisch Milieujaarverslag (e-MJV), aangevuld met enquêtes.

Naast de hoeveelheid afval en wateremissies brengen we ook de milieukosten van bedrijven in kaart, bijvoorbeeld de kosten voor afvalverwerking en voor het lozen van afvalwater. Hiervoor wordt nu een aparte enquête gebruikt. Maar is dat eigenlijk wel nodig?

Tijdens je stage onderzoek je of we de milieukosten voor afval en wateremissies kunnen berekenen met gegevens die al beschikbaar zijn. Je combineert bijvoorbeeld gegevens over de hoeveelheid afval en geloosd water met bestaande indicatoren, zoals gemiddelde kosten per ton afval en sectorspecifieke kosten per kubieke meter geloosd water.

  • bestaande data en indicatoren analyseren en beoordelen op bruikbaarheid;

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Mammography
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Engineering Manager, Mammography leads the engineering team behind Mammo Dx, DeepHealth's FDA- and CE-cleared breast cancer detection AI for 2D mammography and 3D tomosynthesis, within the Clinical AI organization that brings together engineering, AI, clinical, and regulatory teams across the US and Europe. The role also acts as Technical Delivery Manager for the team, owning delivery of every release from plan to production. Working with the Mammo product lead, QRC, and US teams, the Engineering Manager, Mammography ensures the right software reaches the right sites on time, with the quality a medical device requires. The role reports to the Software Engineering Manager, Clinical AI Devices.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead and mentor a team of 3 to 4 engineers; support their technical and professional growth.

  • Set clear goals, run regular 1:1s and performance reviews, and give constructive feedback.

  • Recruit, onboard and retain great engineers.

  • Foster a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement.

Release & Delivery Management (TDM)

  • Own the Mammo release plan jointly with the product lead: scope, sizing, milestones and monthly release tracking.

  • Drive each release end to end: planning, development, verification, regulatory sign-off, deployment and post-release follow-up.

  • Align the Mammo team's delivery practices, processes and tools with the Clinical AI standards.

  • Make sure test setups are ready so product can run functional validation on time.

  • Contribute to the 3- and 6-month roadmap rituals and keep delivery commitments predictable.

Quality & Regulatory Compliance

  • Work with QRC on regulatory impact assessments for every change.

Cross-Functional & US Collaboration

  • Communicate status, risks and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Coordinate with platform, AI and data teams on dependencies.

Technical Leadership

Take part in design and architecture reviews, challenge estimates and unblock the team.

Keep a strong grasp of the system without writing production code day to day.

PLEASE NOTE: This is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and requirements of the position described above. Other functions may be assigned and management retains the right to add or change duties at any time.


Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience (required).

  • 6+ years in software engineering, with a solid technical background (backend, cloud or data-heavy systems) (required).

  • 2+ years managing engineering teams (required).

  • Proven track record delivering software releases end to end: planning, QA, deployment and support (required).

  • Experience running delivery in a structured environment (regulated industry, enterprise B2B or on-premise deployments) (required).

  • Good understanding of modern engineering practices: CI/CD, cloud environments (AWS or GCP), containerized deployments (required).

  • The right to work in France or the Netherlands (required).

  • Strong communication and leadership skills, with a focus on team collaboration and ownership (required).

  • Ability to mentor and organize a team of senior engineers (required).

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills (required).

  • Structured and reliable: people can count on plans and follow-up (required).

  • Comfortable working remotely, asynchronously, and across European and US time zones (required).

  • Fluent in English (required).

  • Preferred: Experience in medical device software (strong plus).

  • Preferred: Knowledge of DICOM and radiology workflows (PACS, RIS, modalities, HL7).

  • Preferred: Experience with radiology AI, ideally mammography.

  • Preferred: Experience working with US-based teams and stakeholders.

Quality Standards

  • Communicates, cooperates, and consistently functions professionally and harmoniously with all levels of supervision, co-workers, visitors, and vendors.

  • Demonstrates initiative, personal awareness, professionalism and integrity, and exercises confidentiality in all areas of performance.· · Follows all local, regional and country laws concerning employment.

  • Follows all DeepHealth policies and procedures.

  • Follows data privacy, compliance, safety and confidentiality standards at all times.

  • Practices universal safety precautions.

  • Promotes good public relations on the phone and in person.

  • Adapts and is willing to learn new tasks, methods, and systems.

  • Reports to work regularly as scheduled; consistently punctual with respect to working hours, meal and rest breaks, and maintains satisfactory personal attendance in accordance with DeepHealth guidelines.

  • Completes job responsibilities in a quality and timely manner.

Travel

  • This position requires domestic and international travel up to 10%, mainly to the US and within Europe.

Working Environment

  • Remote, based in France or the Netherlands. Regular collaboration with US teams requires afternoon overlap with US time zones.

Physical Demands

  • The employee must be able to perform the essential duties and responsibilities of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Paris: 60,000-80,000 EURO

Netherlands: 70,000-90,000 EURO

  • Tracking-Setup & Datensicherheit: Du implementierst und verwaltest Tracking-Setups (z. B. Conversion-APIs, UTM-Konventionen) und stellst eine saubere, datenschutzkonforme Datengrundlage sicher.

  • AI-Expertise (Must-have): Du besitzt praxiserprobte Erfahrung im Einsatz von KI-Tools und LLMs im Marketing-Kontext (z. B. Prompting für Reporting, Analysen, Forecasting). Du verfolgst aktuelle AI-Trends aktiv und brennst darauf, diese bei benuta einzubringen.

  • Hard Skills: Du zeichnest dich durch ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten aus, nutzt GA4 sowie gängige Attributions-/Reporting-Tools souverän und hast tiefe Kenntnisse in mindestens einem Zentralkanal (Google Ads, Meta). Erfahrung mit Bing, Pinterest, Reddit, Affiliate und serverseitigem Tracking runden dein Profil ab.

  • Soft Skills: Du arbeitest datengetrieben, denkst lösungsorientiert und begeisterst dich für E-Commerce sowie die Themen Home & Living.

  • Sprachkompetenz: Deine Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse sind sehr gut (weitere Sprachen sind ein Plus).

Deine Benefits

  • Impact & Gestaltungsspielraum: Bei uns kannst du aktiv mitgestalten, die Marke benuta weiterentwickeln und spannende KI-Projekte umsetzen – wie etwa den Aufbau KI-gestützter Analyse-Workflows für unsere Kampagnendaten. Deine Ideen werden gehört und du bekommst Freiraum für die Umsetzung eigener Ansätze.

  • Präsenz & Flexibilität: Der Schwerpunkt unserer Arbeit liegt auf dem persönlichen Austausch und der gemeinsamen Zusammenarbeit vor Ort an unserem Standort in Berlin. Für die nötige Flexibilität in deiner Alltagsplanung - sei es für private Termine oder ungestörtes Arbeiten - bieten wir dir ein jährliches Kontingent von 26 Home-Office-Tagen.

  • Deine Mobilität: Egal wie du zu uns kommst, wir unterstützen dich. Du hast die Wahl zwischen einem vergünstigten Jobticket oder einer Tankkarte. Zudem bieten wir dir ein Firmenrad-Leasing (JobRad) und eine gute ÖPNV-Anbindung.

  • Zeit für Erholung: Du erhältst 28 Tage Urlaub und profitierst von unserem flexiblen Gleitzeitmodell. Weihnachten und Silvester sind bei uns grundsätzlich arbeitsfreie Tage, die nicht von deinem Urlaubskonto abgehen.

  • Deine Entwicklung: Unsere unterschiedlichen Abteilungen mit internationalen Teams arbeiten an vielfältigen Projekten zusammen. Dadurch lernst Du permanent neue Sichtweisen, Tools und Prozesse kennen – inklusive aktuellster KI-Anwendungen im Performance Marketing.

  • Kultur & Mitarbeitervorteile: Ein strukturiertes Onboarding, flache Hierarchien und attraktive Mitarbeiterrabatte warten auf dich. Bei uns gilt: Come as you are – fühl dich wohl und sei einfach du selbst!

Dein Ansprechpartner ist Michael Stanke (Head of Online Marketing).

*Bei uns zählt der Mensch und seine Motivation - unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion oder sexueller Orientierung. Bewerbungen von Menschen mit einer Schwerbehinderung oder ihnen Gleichgestellten werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt.

Über benuta

Seit 2008 revolutionieren wir von Bonn aus den europäischen Teppich- und Home-&-Living-E-Commerce. Mit über 100 Millionen Euro Umsatz, modernster AI-gestützter Produktinszenierung und Kunden in 17 Ländern verbinden wir die Sicherheit eines etablierten Marktführers mit dem Drive und den flachen Hierarchien eines Digital-Pioneers. Unser Ziel ist einfach: Jedes Zuhause noch schöner zu machen. Werde Teil unseres Teams und hilf uns dabei, noch mehr Menschen für unsere Produkte zu begeistern.

jobs.description:
Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travellers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers including Google Maps and Booking.com.

We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading venture capital investors including TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum, and Northzone, and are headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Penetration Tester to join us as soon as possible. You will run hands-on, authenticated security testing across a real attack surface: public partner-facing booking APIs, payment flows, web and mobile apps used by millions of travellers, and the cloud infrastructure behind them. You’ll plan and run your own testing, work directly with our engineering squads to get findings fixed, and see your impact in production within weeks.

What you will do:

  • Test our partner-facing booking APIs against the OWASP API Security Top 10, with a focus on object- and function-level authorization, tenant isolation, mass assignment, data exposure and rate limiting.

  • Assess API authentication and integrity end to end, including OAuth 2.0/OIDC, API keys, JWTs, webhooks and request signing.

  • Hunt for business-logic abuse in booking, checkout, payment and refund flows, including race conditions and pricing manipulation.

  • Run authenticated tests of traveller-, partner- and operator-facing web and mobile apps following OWASP WSTG and ASVS, including how passenger personal data is stored, shown and exported.

  • Review cloud, Kubernetes and CI/CD configurations and secrets handling for attack paths that could be chained from an application bug.

  • Map and regularly test our internet-facing attack surface.

  • Red-team our AI features (assistants, agents, support bots) against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

  • Write clear, reproducible, risk-rated findings with practical remediation guidance, walk engineers through fixes and verify them with retests.

Workplace:

We are a remote-first company with teams located around the Globe and a HQ in Berlin.


Who you are:

  • You bring 5+ years of hands-on penetration testing, mainly of web applications and APIs, and can point to recent engagements you’ve led end to end.

  • You have deep, practical knowledge of the OWASP API Security Top 10, WSTG and ASVS, including authentication/authorization models (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT), IDOR/BOLA, mass assignment, SSRF, injection and XSS.

  • You have found business-logic and race-condition vulnerabilities in transactional systems such as booking, e-commerce, payments or fintech.

  • You are fluent with Burp Suite Pro (or similar) and write your own scripts and tooling (Python, Go or similar).

  • You are comfortable assessing cloud and container environments (GCP preferred, Kubernetes) and CI/CD pipelines.

  • You work independently: you scope, prioritise, test and report with minimal guidance, and you explain complex risks plainly to engineers and leadership.

  • You are available to start at short notice.

  • Bonus Points: OSCP, OSWE, BSCP or similar certifications; experience red-teaming LLM applications or AI agents; testing in PCI-DSS environments.

What you can expect:

  • You will join a fast-paced travel tech company with a flat organizational structure.

  • You will have exciting opportunities, ownership, and responsibility and contribute directly to the success of the company.

  • You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support and challenge you every day!

  • We have a flexible work policy with the option of working remotely and international opportunities arising as we continue to expand our global footprint – Our heart is in Berlin, but you’ll find us across the globe.

  • You will get a competitive salary.

jobs.title: Software Engineer (80-100%)
jobs.description:
Worum geht es?

Wenn in der Schweiz eine Feuerwehr alarmiert wird, läuft die Meldung mit hoher Wahrscheinlichkeit über unsere Systeme. Rund 400 Feuerwehren in 16 Kantonen arbeiten mit unseren Lösungen, von der Alarmierung über die Einsatzführung bis zur Einsatzplanung.

Das heisst: Unsere Software muss funktionieren, auch nachts um 3 Uhr. Diese Verantwortung prägt, wie wir entwickeln.

Wir suchen dich als Software Engineer, der unsere Plattform mitträgt. Nicht als weitere Person im Team, sondern als eine tragende Säule in unserem Team.

Über uns

Die EvoSys AG wurde 2011 gegründet und entwickelt seit 2016 eigene Software für Behörden und Organisationen für Rettung und Sicherheit (BORS). Wir sind ein inhabergeführtes Familienunternehmen in Thun mit 9 Mitarbeitenden und in unserem Markt führend.

Unsere Produkte heissen AlarmHub, Intervento, FloriPlan, AlarmDisplay und SpotPilot. Sie decken den ganzen Ablauf ab, von der Alarmierung bis zur Auswertung nach dem Einsatz. 2028 kommt mit Respondo eine weitere Lösung dazu.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst unsere bestehenden Plattformen weiter und setzt neue Funktionen von der Idee bis in den Betrieb um.

  • Du prägst unsere Architektur mit. Unsere Kundenbasis wächst stark, und unsere Systeme müssen mitwachsen. Konkret bereiten wir den Schritt auf Kubernetes vor und bauen Dienste so um, dass sie zuverlässig skalieren.

  • Du arbeitest an Schnittstellen zu Einsatzzentralen, Partnersystemen und Behördenplattformen.

  • Du setzt KI-gestützte Werkzeuge im Entwicklungsalltag ein, so wie wir alle.

  • Du nimmst an Code Reviews teil und trägst zu Qualität und Dokumentation bei.

  • Du unterstützt bei anspruchsvollen technischen Fragen aus dem Betrieb.

Perspektive

Mit der Zeit kannst du die fachliche Verantwortung für einen Produktbereich übernehmen. Und wenn es für beide Seiten passt, ist längerfristig auch eine technische Führungsrolle denkbar. Solche Rollen besetzen wir aus dem Team heraus. Voraussetzung für diese Stelle ist das aber ausdrücklich nicht.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Rund 2 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Entwicklung von Webanwendungen. Die ersten Jahre hast du hinter dir und arbeitest selbständig, ohne enge Begleitung.

  • Erfahrung mit Node.js und Vue.js, dazu Berührungspunkte mit PostgreSQL, Docker, Linux und Git.

  • Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge selbstverständlich und kannst beurteilen, wann du ihrem Ergebnis trauen kannst und wann nicht.

  • Verständnis dafür, was im Produktivsystem passiert, wenn dein Code dort ankommt.

Art direction and creation

Brand identity

Production and collaboration

  • Adapt creations across formats and languages, down to the final production file, in line with the Brand Book.
  • Collaborate closely with the motion designer and 3D artist, and share your practices with the graphic design apprentice.

You have at least 4 years of experience in art direction or graphic design, gained in an agency, an in-house studio or a brand.

Nice to have

  • Motion design (After Effects), video editing or 3D skills.
  • Experience in health or wellness.

How you work

Benefits

  • Working in an international environment, with teams based in Issy-les-Moulineaux, Boston, Hong Kong and Shenzhen, among other locations.

  • A small, close-knit team where your voice counts.
  • Room to explore new tools, AI and ways of working, where your ideas and experiments matter as much as production.
